clue.text: I need the end of good to turn me on

definitions.text: I need the end of good to turn me on

indicators.note: the end of a word is its final letter, so only the closing letter of good is used
to turn the words me on is to twist their letters round into a new order

explanation.surface: Someone confesses that a final bit of goodness is what arouses them.
explanation.walkthrough: 'the end of' takes D from good; 'to turn' rearranges ME ON into EMON. Read as a whole, the clue is the fiend speaking: it needs good to end before it comes alive.
explanation.definitionFit: A fiend or evil spirit is roused when goodness is finished, so the whole sentence describes such a devil.

clue.text: Contractions of Wells manuscript

parts.note: wells, like mineral springs, are spas

explanation.surface: An abridged version of a manuscript by the author H. G. Wells.
explanation.walkthrough: Wells looks like the novelist, but it is plural springs, SPAS.
explanation.definitionFit: Spasms are involuntary muscle contractions, such as cramps.

clue.text: Nutty biscuits

explanation.surface: Biscuits flavoured with nuts.
explanation.definitionFit: Crackers is slang for mad or nutty, and crackers are also thin dry savoury biscuits.

clue.text: Concentrate on where one lives

explanation.surface: Focusing on one's home.
explanation.definitionFit: To address a problem is to turn one's attention to it; one's address is the home location for post.

clue.text: Changing of the guard-a female issue?

indicators.note: changing of signals that the letters of the following words are altered into a fresh order

explanation.surface: Wondering whether the ceremony at Buckingham Palace is a matter for women.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Changing of' rearranges THE GUARD. The Changing of the Guard is a famous London ceremony at Buckingham Palace; 'issue' means offspring, not a problem.
explanation.definitionFit: Issue means offspring, and a female child is a girl born to her parents.

clue.text: Overlooking in aid of charity

parts.note: for means in aid of, as in a collection for a cause
charity is the giving of help to those in need

explanation.surface: Ignoring something while raising money for good causes.
explanation.definitionFit: Overlooking a fault is pardoning it, being merciful about it.

clue.text: Reckless road-speed is criminal

definitions.note: an adjective standing for a reckless person, the noun

indicators.note: something criminal is crooked or bent, so the letters of road-speed are bent out of shape

explanation.surface: Driving at a dangerous pace on the road is against the law.
explanation.walkthrough: 'is criminal' rearranges ROADSPEED. The definition is loose: a reckless outlaw, the noun, rather than the adjective.
explanation.definitionFit: A desperado is a reckless, violent outlaw ready to take any risk.

clue.text: Breed of sheep to keep Bill in work!

indicators.note: in places the bill inside the word for work

parts.note: a job is a piece of work
AC, short for account, is a bill

explanation.surface: A farmer keeps a breed of sheep to make sure there is work for someone called Bill.
explanation.walkthrough: Bill is not a name but an account; 'to keep' is surface padding before the container signal 'in'.
explanation.definitionFit: The Jacob is a piebald, often four-horned, sheep breed.

clue.text: Fellows take a day to get better

parts.note: fellows are men

explanation.surface: The men need a day off to recover.
explanation.definitionFit: To mend is to heal or recover, as a broken bone does.

clue.text: Dramatic desire say, to have no mechanical power?

definitions.text: Dramatic desire say, to have no mechanical power?

parts.words: Dramatic desire say, to have no mechanical power?
parts.note: Shakespeare's Richard III cries out for a horse on stage, the dramatic desire; add a vehicle pulled by that animal and it has no engine

explanation.surface: A theatrical longing that leaves one without an engine.
explanation.walkthrough: In Shakespeare's Richard III the king cries 'A horse! A horse! My kingdom for a horse!'. A tram or carriage drawn by that animal has no mechanical power.
explanation.definitionFit: A horse-drawn tram running on rails, pulled by an animal instead of an engine.

clue.text: Take on commission

explanation.surface: Hiring someone on a commission basis.
explanation.definitionFit: To engage staff is to take them on or hire them; to engage an artist is to commission work from them.

clue.text: Youth, for example, lies about

indicators.note: about signals that the letters of lies are turned around into a new order

explanation.surface: Young people, as a rule, tell fibs.
explanation.walkthrough: 'about' rearranges LIES. Youth is not young people but the Isle of Youth, an island off Cuba.
explanation.definitionFit: The Isle of Youth (Isla de la Juventud) is a Cuban island, an example of an islet.

clue.text: Sleeping pill collected about tea-time

indicators.note: about means the word for collected goes round the tea-time letters

parts.note: collected means calm, sedate
four o'clock is tea-time, and four is IV in Roman numerals

explanation.surface: Someone picked up a sleeping pill at around tea-time.
explanation.walkthrough: Tea-time is traditionally four o'clock in Britain, so the time stands for its Roman numeral.
explanation.definitionFit: A sedative is a calming drug, such as a sleeping tablet.

clue.text: Notice way of speaking as a habit

parts.note: an ad, an advertisement, is a notice
diction is a manner of speaking or enunciating

explanation.surface: Someone notices that a way of speaking has become habitual.
explanation.definitionFit: An addiction is a compulsive habit, such as a drug habit.

clue.text: Eastern house dish sometimes preferred to sultanas?

definitions.text: Eastern house dish sometimes preferred to sultanas?

parts.words: Eastern house dish sometimes preferred to sultanas?
parts.note: a dish is slang for an attractive woman, and in an Eastern ruler's household such a slave girl might be favoured over the sultan's wives

explanation.surface: A Middle Eastern restaurant dish that some prefer to dried fruit.
explanation.walkthrough: Dish and sultanas look like food; a dish is an attractive woman and sultanas are a sultan's wives, so this is a harem concubine.
explanation.definitionFit: A slave girl or concubine in a Turkish harem, sometimes favoured above the sultan's wives.

clue.text: Pop article in French daily

indicators.note: in puts the article inside the name of the French daily paper

parts.note: Le Monde is a daily newspaper in France
a is the indefinite article

explanation.surface: A fizzy drink featured in a Paris newspaper.
explanation.definitionFit: Pop is a fizzy soft drink, and lemonade is the classic example.

clue.text: It is an offence to have a loud van

parts.note: F, forte, is the musical direction for loud
the van, short for vanguard, is the front

explanation.surface: Owning a noisy delivery van is against the law.
explanation.walkthrough: Van is not a vehicle but the vanguard, the front.
explanation.definitionFit: An affront is an insult that causes offence.

clue.text: Writer whose work is catching

explanation.surface: An author whose writing is infectious.
explanation.walkthrough: Henry Fielding wrote Tom Jones; in cricket, fielding is the work of the side not batting, and much of it is catching the ball.
explanation.definitionFit: Henry Fielding was an English novelist; fielding in cricket or baseball involves stopping and catching the ball.

clue.text: Compete in attempt to make fine pattern

indicators.note: in puts the word for compete inside the attempt

parts.note: a try is an attempt
to race is to compete

explanation.surface: Competing in an attempt to make a delicate design.
explanation.definitionFit: Tracery is delicate ornamental stonework or pattern, as in Gothic windows.

clue.text: Coats sailor used as Mae West, for example

parts.note: films are thin coats or layers
tar is a traditional word for a sailor

explanation.surface: A sailor's coat serves as a life jacket, which wartime airmen called a Mae West.
explanation.walkthrough: A Mae West was RAF slang for an inflatable life jacket, which suits the surface; here it is the Hollywood actress.
explanation.definitionFit: Mae West was a celebrated Hollywood actress of the 1930s.

clue.text: Fairly big order

explanation.surface: A sizeable command.
explanation.definitionFit: A tidy sum is a fairly large amount; to tidy is to put things in order.

clue.text: Soft piece of cake

explanation.surface: A slice of sponge.
explanation.definitionFit: Easy can mean soft or lenient, as in an easy touch; a piece of cake is something simple to do.

clue.text: Battered wives' left turn

indicators.note: battered means knocked about, so the letters of wives are beaten into a new order

explanation.surface: Abused wives finally turn left and leave.
explanation.definitionFit: To swivel is to pivot or rotate.

clue.text: Value of some game ritual

indicators.note: some says the answer is a run of letters hidden inside the words that follow

parts.note: the letters run across the end of one word into the next

explanation.surface: Questioning what worth there is in a game's ceremony.
explanation.definitionFit: Merit is worth or excellence.

clue.text: Made amends for when mouse ran up clock by day

parts.note: in the nursery rhyme Hickory Dickory Dock, the mouse ran up the clock and the clock struck one: that happened at one

explanation.surface: Someone made amends after a mouse ran up the clock during the day.
explanation.walkthrough: In the nursery rhyme 'Hickory Dickory Dock' the clock struck one after the mouse ran up, so this was AT ONE.
explanation.definitionFit: To atone for a wrong is to make amends or reparation for it.

clue.text: Does he have dual controls taking fish to water

definitions.note: a question standing for the person who has them, a noun

parts.note: cod is a fish
a river is a body of water

explanation.surface: Asking whether a learner's car with two sets of pedals is used to take fish to the river.
explanation.walkthrough: Dual controls suggest a driving instructor's car; a rally co-driver shares the driving.
explanation.definitionFit: A co-driver shares the driving of a vehicle, taking turns at the wheel.

clue.text: Poet without merit in the things he says

indicators.note: without means the word for merit is taken away from the poet's name

parts.note: William Wordsworth was a famous English Romantic poet
worth is merit or value

explanation.surface: A poet with no talent shows it in his utterances.
explanation.walkthrough: The poet is William Wordsworth; 'without' drops WORTH from his name.
explanation.definitionFit: Words are utterances, what someone says.
